'''Nicolas Grandjean''' (born February 14, 1967) is a French and Swiss professor of [[physics]]. His achievements include over 600 articles.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=yY7bfPQAAAAJ&hl&hl=en&oi=ao|title=Nicolas Grandjean|publisher=[[Google Scholar]]|accessdate=November 1, 2024}}</ref>

==Biography==
Nicolas Grandjean was born in [[Dijon]], [[France]], and is a French and Swiss citizen. He studied at the [[University of Clermont-Ferrand]] and the [[Université Nice-Sophia-Antipolis]]. In 1991, he joined the Solid-State Physics and Solar Energy Laboratory, a division of the [[French National Center for Scientific Research]] where he studied semiconductor nanostructures. By 1994 he obtained his Ph.D. Later on, as a senior research fellow, he worked at the [[Research Center for Heteroepitaxy and its Applications]], a division of CNRS in [[Sophia Antipolis]].

In 2004, he became a tenure-track professor at the [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne]] becoming a director of the [[Laboratory of Advanced Semiconductors for Photonics and Electronics]] where he still serves.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.epfl.ch/labs/laspe/|author=École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne|title=Advanced Semiconductors for Photonics and Electronics|publisher=École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne|accessdate=November 1, 2024}}</ref> He was promoted Full Professor in 2010.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.myscience.ch/en/news/wire/nicolas_grandjean_nomme_professeur_ordinaire-epfl|title=Nicolas Grandjean nommé professeur ordinaire|publisher=myScience|date=December 11, 2009|accessdate=November 1, 2024}}</ref> From 2012 to 2016, he was the director of the Institute of Condensed Matter.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://infoscience.epfl.ch/entities/orgunit/c1d69cbc-68f9-43bc-ad79-ad2488d57003|title=Institute of Condensed Matter Physics|publisher=École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne|accessdate=November 1, 2024}}</ref> From 2019 to 2026, he was a board member of Riber,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.riber.com/finance/governance/|title=Governance|publisher=[[Riber]]|accessdate=November 1, 2024}}</ref> a world's leading supplier of Molecular Beam Epitaxy (MBE) products.

In January 2025, he was appointed Associate Vice-President for Education at EPFL.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://newsletter.epfl.ch/en/newsletters/2a587a8d-a4be-4719-ba26-ad7d547040f9/render/|title=Internal EPFL Newsletter|publisher=EPFL|date=October 2024|accessdate=November 20, 2025}}</ref> In September 2026, the ETH Board appointed him to the Direction of EPFL as Vice President for Education.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://ethrat.ch/en/fit-for-the-future-shared-roof-for-the-research-institutes/|title=FIT for the Future: Shared roof for the research institutes|publisher=ETH Board|date=September 24, 2026|access-date=November 8, 2026}}</ref>

==Research==
In 1999, he along with his colleagues, have discovered that combining [[gallium nitride]] (GaN) and [[quantum dot]]s (QDs) into [[aluminum nitride]] (AIN) matrix, produces a glowing white light.<ref>{{cite journal|author1=B. Damilano |author2=Nicolas Grandjean |author3=F. Semond |author4=J. Massies |author5=M. Leroux |title=From visible to white light emission by GaN quantum dots on Si(111) substrate|journal=[[Applied Physics Letters]]|volume=75|issue=7|pages=962–964|date=June 18, 2009|doi=10.1063/1.124567|bibcode=1999ApPhL..75..962D}}</ref> In 2006, his group and colleagues at the University of Southampton reported polariton lasing at room-temperature.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevLett.98.126405|title=Room-Temperature Polariton Lasing in Semiconductor Microcavities|publisher=Purpose-Led Publishing|date=March 21, 2007|accessdate=November 1, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nature.com/articles/447540a|title=A polatiton laser|publisher=nature|date=May 30, 2007|accessdate=November 1, 2024}}</ref>
